source_policy_evidence.section: General Questions: Is content on sec.gov free? Do I need permission to reuse EDGAR content?
source_policy_evidence.finding: The SEC states that Government-created content on sec.gov and EDGAR public filing content are free to access and reuse. The same page sets the fair-access rule: scripted access is allowed with a declared User-Agent, at no more than 10 requests per second.
source_policy_evidence.verification: Official page opened and read on 2026-11-01 by the seat; consistent with the 2026-10-19 reading recorded in SEC-PUBLIC-FILING-FACT-USE-20261019.

source_policy_evidence.finding: Information on the SEC website may be copied or further distributed without SEC permission; users are asked to cite the SEC as the source; the SEC seal, logos and artwork are not to be used; SEC and EDGAR marks may be referred to in text only without implying affiliation or approval.
source_policy_evidence.verification: Official page opened and read on 2026-11-01 by the seat.

source_class.description: The issuer's own EX-99.1 earnings-release exhibit of a Form 8-K or 8-K/A that reports Item 2.02, fetched from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/<issuer cik>/ under the fair-access rule and recorded with its original first-retrieval receipt and sha256.
source_class.document_identity: exact archive URL plus retained sha256; one runtime grant per document
source_class.identity_rule: The EDGAR filing index lists the document with Type exactly EX-99.1; the filer CIK in the archive path equals the issuer's CIK for the ticker; the form is 8-K or 8-K/A reporting Item 2.02. File-name matching alone never qualifies a document, and an EX-99.2 or 8-K main document gets no grant.
source_class.byte_retention: none: document bytes are held in memory only for the cycle that hashes and parses them; the writer persists the URL, sha256, figures, filing clock and first-retrieval receipt id
excluded: any exhibit other than the issuer's EX-99.1 earnings release
third-party documents filed under the same /Archives/ prefix (consents, opinions, reports by others)
SEC-generated index pages as a display source
any document not present in the pinned catalyst source snapshot

permitted_use.channel: web display on /api/catalyst and /api/catalyst/scan, plus link-only partner pack
permitted_use.attribution_text: <Issuer>, Form 8-K Item 2.02 EX-99.1, filed with the SEC, with a link to the original sec.gov archive document
permitted_use.display_facts: only figures and clocks verified against the document bytes at retrieval, with the sha256 recorded

scope_limits: Facts stated by the issuer are displayed with attribution and a link to the original; no expression from the release is quoted, excerpted, rehosted or exported.

Copyright in issuer-authored exhibits stays with the issuer (they are not 17 U.S.C. 105 works); this basis relies on fact-only display plus the SEC reuse policy, not on a claim that the text is public domain.
No SEC seal, logo, artwork or trademark branding, and no wording that implies SEC affiliation, endorsement or approval.
No email, scheduled send, partner rehost or paid-product use is admitted by this record; each needs its own consent or rights decision.
Grants are minted per exact document by marketing.catalyst_source_adapter and expire at min(first retrieval + 7 days, mint time + 24 hours).

This is a documented source-policy review by the seat, not a Chairman grant, legal opinion, vendor license or economic-truth ruling. It does not extend DEC:COMMERCIAL-DATA-RIGHTS-CHAIRMAN-ATTESTATION-20261023, which does not name SEC EDGAR.
No live publication is established by this record; the public flags stay off until their operator turns them on.
